gold: Every changed non-controller expect-based test has exactly one direct expect proving its intended observable contract without hidden assertions or synthetic bundles. Controller tests retain meaningful direct status/body assertions, and native node:assert tests retain their framework. Independent saves and outcomes remain independently visible with concrete expectations; required transition, race, and rollback evidence is preserved. Structural compliance alone never proves semantic quality.

rubric.question: Review every complete changed test in the supplied scope, not only edited lines. If the changed-test scope is missing or incomplete, return BLOCKED with the exact missing evidence.

Apply exactly one direct expect per non-controller expect-based test as the shared default, not a local opt-in or at-most-one rule: zero and multiple calls violate it. Asymmetric matcher factories are not additional direct expect calls. Preserve native node:assert/assert/strict assertions rather than requiring a framework migration; native assertions elsewhere in a file do not exempt an expect-based test or an assertion-free test. Identify governing ordinary-language local standards and cite their source; report genuine conflicts truthfully. If required guidance is unavailable, return BLOCKED rather than guessing.

Assess whether the single expectation proves the named behavior through a natural real result or meaningful native matcher. Preserve native promise rejection assertions, web-first matchers, meaningful nested matchers, and direct comparisons of actual returned, fetched, or persisted objects and arrays. Prefer a complete natural contract such as a route fullPath where appropriate. Reject fabricated summary objects, weakened payloads, and bundled .mock.calls; exact count alone is not semantic proof.

Identify independent outcomes or saves bundled in one test, and assertions hidden in Arrange, Act, helpers, or hooks. Independent saves need separate focused tests using API spies and concrete expected payloads, not expect.anything() payloads or bundled call arrays. Preserve transition/race/rollback setup, causal sequences, and scenario identities in each focused test that needs them; do not remove earlier operations or weaken observations to satisfy count. Inspect invoked helpers and relevant scenario context when needed; if required context is unavailable, return BLOCKED. Irrelevant absent callers or optional siblings are not required context.

Apply the controller exception only to paths with a controller/ or controllers/ directory segment (case-insensitive), or filenames ending .controller.test/spec.<JS/TS extension>, -controller.test/spec.<extension>, _controller.test/spec.<extension>, or Controller.test/spec.<extension> with the PascalCase suffix. Never infer controller status from HTTP usage or a response variable. Preserve clear direct status/body controller assertions or a meaningful response matcher; keep independent persistence effects separate. A coupled invariant is not a general multi-expect exception for non-controller tests, and allow-multiple-expects is not a bypass. Preserve supported explicit scoped suppressions. Each finding must cite the test and governing guidance, identify the count violation or semantic gap, and offer a concrete correction without inventing findings.
